name: Non-involuting Congenital Hemangioma

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Clinical and Imaging Diagnostic Criteria for NICH

criteria.description: Presence of a fully formed vascular lesion at birth
Lack of significant regression or involution of the lesion over time
Characteristic imaging findings on Doppler ultrasound or MRI showing high-flow vascular channels without involution features
Histopathologic confirmation showing lobular capillary proliferation with GLUT1 negativity

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of a congenital vascular lesion with no involution and characteristic imaging findings
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Histopathology is supportive but not always required if clinical and imaging criteria are definitive.

laboratory: Normal or mildly decreased platelet count in some cases
Coagulation profile usually normal unless Kasabach-Merritt phenomenon present
imaging: Doppler ultrasound showing high-flow vascular channels without involution
MRI demonstrating well-circumscribed lobulated vascular mass with prominent flow voids
genetic: GLUT1 negativity distinguishes from infantile hemangioma
No known specific genetic mutation identified
other: Histopathology shows lobular capillary proliferation with large, dilated vessels
Absence of endothelial cell proliferation markers typical of infantile hemangioma

distinguishingFeatures: Typically appears postnatally rather than fully formed at birth
Lesion present at birth but undergoes rapid involution within first year
Similar imaging but different clinical course
Usually present at birth but grows proportionally with child
No spontaneous involution or rapid growth phase

redFlags: Rapid lesion growth with ulceration and bleeding
references: Enjolras O, Mulliken JB. Vascular tumors and vascular malformations (new issues). Adv Dermatol. 1997;13:375-423.
Haggstrom AN, Drolet BA, Baselga E, et al. Prospective study of infantile hemangiomas: clinical characteristics predicting complications and treatment. Pediatrics. 2006;118(3):882-887.
